title: Acetazolamide and bicarbonate-dependent excitation
opening_paragraph: **Question before measuring.** Revisit the laboratory's pH work from the perspective of GABA currents and developmental stage. Can acetazolamide reduce the late depolarizing response to repeated GABAergic stimulation in WWOX-deficient neurons without simply suppressing the entire network through acidification? The laboratory has already tracked changes in extracellular pH after the drug. The new comparison asks whether intracellular bicarbonate regeneration, chloride loading or bulk acidification limits the response. title: N-acetylcysteine: substrate rescue or a misleading culture background?
opening_paragraph: **Question.** Does providing cysteine restore glutathione synthesis and a neural function in WWOX loss, or does substrate handling change extracellular glutamate or network firing while the developmental defect persists? Tissue redox markers, reduced glutathione, glutathione synthesis and cystine–glutamate exchange are different outcomes. Keep NAC uptake and deacetylation, extracellular thiol chemistry, glial uptake and neuronal response distinct. Revisit the laboratory's [earlier redox hypothesis](../../rs_r6_it30_20261106/hypotheses.md) and its [prior medium audit](../../myelin_premises_20261108/verify/items.md).
labelled_decision_paragraphs: **Disposition: retain as a mechanistic probe, park for trial prioritization.** Concordant uptake and exchange transcripts, discordant nuclear clearance and a direct biphasic response support a specific neuron–astrocyte test. Reopen for genotype-selective isotope incorporation plus functional recovery at measured exposure, with simultaneous glutamate and firing measurements. [WWOX data, counterexamples and reopening criterion](mechanism.md) · [Pediatric feasibility and exposure](exposure.md)

title: Calcium alpha-ketoglutarate and oxygen sensing in WWOX loss
opening_paragraph: **Opening prediction.** WWOX loss can change HIF-1α regulation in fibroblasts. These facts raise a conditional question: at physiological oxygen and equal calcium, does added non-esterified alpha-ketoglutarate reach the relevant neural compartment and increase HIF hydroxylation before glycolysis changes? There is no measured CNS exposure to oral calcium alpha-ketoglutarate in these results. Do not equate the approximately 14 µM arterial increment with cytosolic concentration, or the adult calcium-matched bone trial with a pediatric pharmacokinetic study. Ester preparations can hydrolyze outside cells and influence pH or respiration independently. title: D-β-hydroxybutyrate, substrate supply and M-current
opening_paragraph: **Question.** Does adding the endogenous D enantiomer increase the neuronal KCNQ2/3 M-current at the background ketone exposure already present in WWOX? The alternative is that any functional gain follows oxidation as a fuel, differences in cell type or broader effects of ketogenic nutrition. This refers to one defined molecule. The WWOX cohort documents exposure to a ketogenic diet, which changes multiple metabolites; its outcome cannot be attributed to exogenous D-BHB. [Held dietary ascertainment](../triheptanoin/comparators.md)
queue_checkpoint_paragraph: **D-β-hydroxybutyrate parked for pediatric trial priority.** The robust signal in human open data is stimulus-dependent evoked cortical gain on the native amplitude scale. title: D-biotin and glial maturation in WWOX loss
opening_paragraph: **Prespecified before opening the WWOX expression results.** D-biotin is a cofactor shared by acetyl-CoA carboxylases and pyruvate carboxylase. A limiting fraction of biotinylated ACC1 in surviving WWOX-deficient oligodendrocytes could reduce fatty-acid synthesis during new sheath formation. Alternatively, extra biotin could act through astrocyte pyruvate carboxylation and substrate supply, or improve survival without restoring myelin function. A positive control with an established biotin-dependent defect can verify the response assay. Untreated transcript abundance cannot establish cofactor occupancy.
labelled_decision_paragraphs: **Human transfer and interim decision.** Adult progressive MS is a limited comparator for developmental WWOX disease. In SPI2, 39/326 improved on pharmaceutical-grade biotin versus 29/316 on placebo. The authors report OR 1.35 (95% CI 0.81–2.26). Biotin interfered with some clinical laboratory tests despite mitigation. The rat fiber result therefore supports a cellular hypothesis, while the human data give little basis for extrapolating a functional effect. Keep D-biotin at the preclinical evidence stage. A single  || **Closed for this cycle.** [Drug-specific pediatric comparison, longitudinal limits and reopening criterion](decision.md).

Pediatric drug cohorts suggest altered metabolism in selected exposures but do not establish persistent cerebral deficiency. [Decision and secondary-deficiency comparison](d_biotin/decision.md)

The WWOX datasets already implicate altered oxidative metabolism and an unstable direction for the shared vitamin transporter SLC5A6 across species. D-pantothenate is a precursor for coenzyme A (CoA). The hypothesis is that deficient free mitochondrial CoA limits oxidation of pyruvate or fatty acids in WWOX-deficient neural cells. Alternatives include limited pantothenate phosphorylation, altered mitochondrial CoA import and sequestration of CoA in acyl-CoA specie
labelled_decision_paragraphs: **Closed for this cycle.** [Residual kinase, oral pharmacokinetics, direct human CSF measurement, pediatric limits and reopening criterion](decision.md).

title: L-lysine hydrochloride and neuronal lysine availability
opening_paragraph: **Selection and prespecified alternatives.** Neuronal Wwox knockdown reduced an identified essential amino acid in fly heads. A supply-limited model predicts that free L-lysine and the fraction of charged lysyl-tRNA both fall in untreated, developmentally matched mammalian WWOX neural cells. Under this model restoring substrate should restore charging and nascent protein synthesis at matched cell viability. Higher protein turnover, increased catabolism, altered cell composition or competition at a transporter could instead lower the tissue pool while charging remains sufficient. Total tissue lysine cannot distinguish these mechanisms. This is

title: L-serine and the decision between membrane synthesis and excitatory co-agonism
opening_paragraph: **Opening prediction, before the RNA comparison.** Juvenile WWOX models show defects in ensheathment and cell development. If a local shortage of L-serine for membrane lipid synthesis contributes, uptake of supplied L-serine into canonical sphingoid bases should precede improved functional ensheathment. Compare an isogenic corrected preparation at the same age, activity and viable lineage-cell count. An increase restricted to total serine or the number of precursors would not establish functional rescue. The same precursor may supply D-serine, a co-agonist at NMDA receptors. queue_checkpoint_paragraph: **L-serine parked for pediatric WWOX trial priority.** The mouse astroglial PHGDH signal survives depth matching. title: Lacosamide, sustained discharges and axonal development
opening_paragraph: **Question before inspecting the WWOX target contrasts.** An antiseizure medicine that preferentially reduces sustained firing could dampen prolonged WWOX discharges while leaving the first spikes of a physiological response intact. But if it reduces recruitment of inhibitory neurons or propagation in already hypomyelinated axons, the same drug could narrow the usable range of the network. Test event initiation, total duration, inhibitory-cell recruitment and stimulus-evoked conduction separately. The primary comparison is genotype by firing history at comparable unbound exposure and baseline activity, with independent preparations as replica
labelled_decision_paragraphs: **Disposition.** Park for WWOX-specific trial prioritization. The human tissue endpoint conditions on prolonged firing, and the juvenile WWOX resting-voltage shifts differ across cell classes and control groups. Reopen for preserved inhibitory recruitment and conduction during a selective, exposure-matched response on native brief discharges. [Timing, human-cell selection and genotype comparator](timing.md)
queue_checkpoint_paragraph: **Lacosamide parked for WWOX trial prioritization.** Human tissue evidence concerns prolonged firing, with the waveform analysis restricted to persistent spikes under drug. Juvenile WWOX data support measuring distinct cell types at native and matched starting voltage. [Contrasts, exposure and reopening criteria](lacosamide/timing.md)

title: Lamotrigine, dendritic excitation and inhibitory recruitment
opening_paragraph: **Reason to select this AED.** WWOX neuronal-deletion mice have abnormal cortical recruitment. The shared HCN analysis already considered inhibition of the current with ivabradine. Lamotrigine provides a different question about a possible increase in dendritic HCN current alongside use-dependent sodium-channel inhibition. Pyramidal dendrites and the interneurons that target them may respond differently. queue_checkpoint_paragraph: **Lamotrigine parked for WWOX pediatric trial prioritization.** At 3 µM the juvenile cortical field response falls with the number of detectable sites. title: Levetiracetam, zinc-sensitive receptor currents and vesicle release
opening_paragraph: **Why this molecule follows topiramate.** A positive WWOX observation on levetiracetam plus topiramate cannot distinguish the two agents. Other laboratory work has already counted exposures, analyzed brivaracetam occupancy and considered activity-dependent presynaptic effects. Use those records without counting combination outcomes twice. This analysis focuses on a separate reported property of levetiracetam: reversal of an imposed negative allosteric modulation of inhibitory receptor currents. Endogenous extracellular zinc sufficient to engage this mechanism in WWOX remains a hypothesis. [Existing audit](../topiramate/clinical_timeline.md) ·
labelled_decision_paragraphs: **Disposition.** The pediatric trial and audited WWOX histories support retaining a focal-seizure hypothesis. Park for an unselected WWOX trial. [Pediatric analysis and conditions to reopen](pediatric.md)

title: Levocarnitine and substrate use in WWOX deficiency
opening_paragraph: **Prediction recorded before measuring the WWOX contrasts.** If the limiting defect is insufficient cellular free L-carnitine, restoration of that pool should preferentially improve long-chain fatty acid oxidation compared with a carnitine-shuttle-independent substrate in the affected cell type. If the limiting defect lies at mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation downstream of the shuttle, or in shared respiration, increasing the free pool may leave oxidation unchanged. Plasma free carnitine and acyl-to-free ratios alone cannot distinguish these mechanisms. Compare age, dietary intake, tissue, baseline free carnitine and valproate exposure. Impr

queue_checkpoint_paragraph: **Levocarnitine parked for trial prioritization.** A randomized pediatric valproate study supports a short-term difference in ammonia. title: Magnesium chloride and voltage-dependent NMDA current in WWOX
opening_paragraph: **Opening question.** A prior sulforaphane culture comparison induced epileptiform activity by removing magnesium. Reversal of that manipulation can occur in control neurons. Select magnesium chloride as an oral mineral candidate and identify the effective species as extracellular ionized Mg²⁺. Establish whether the WWOX preparation has an abnormal response within a physiological range. Adult intravenous sulfate studies can constrain compartment interpretation only; oral chloride requires its own pediatric exposure evidence.
labelled_decision_paragraphs: **Final disposition.** Park for an unselected trial. The [exposure, channel estimates and WWOX endpoint audit](csf.md) specify the controls and criteria for reopening.

opening_paragraph: **Prediction recorded before the WWOX comparison.** The relevant substrate is myo-inositol. opening_paragraph: **Opening prediction.** Revisit the laboratory's prior abstention on lipoate with one defined compound, free R-alpha-lipoic acid. opening_paragraph: **Question before inspecting the WWOX expression panel.** Does WWOX loss limit conversion of free riboflavin to FMN or FAD, delivery to mitochondria, or the ability of a flavoprotein to retain its cofactor? title: Triheptanoin and replenishment of the WWOX tricarboxylic acid cycle
opening_paragraph: **Why this molecule.** The laboratory previously used triheptanoin as a fuel comparator for altered pyruvate dehydrogenase signaling. A generic developmental-epilepsy drug ranking also returned it, with little disease specificity. The new question is whether odd-chain carbon can specifically restore a depleted cerebral cycle intermediate pool. A rise in ketone availability or provision of extra calories might account for improved function independently. title: Uridine triacetate and pyrimidine availability in WWOX loss
opening_paragraph: **Candidate choice and scientific premise.** Uridine triacetate is an oral prodrug of uridine. title: Vigabatrin, inhibitory transmission and mitochondrial nucleotide salvage
opening_paragraph: **Opening prediction.** Revisit this antiepileptic through a second function of its target, mitochondrial GABA transaminase (ABAT). Sustained impairment of nucleotide supply could limit mtDNA maintenance during repeated activation in energetically vulnerable WWOX cells even if GABA breakdown and spontaneous bursts fall. A rival is reversible network suppression with preserved mitochondrial function after activity is matched. Test GABA-T activity, dNTP pools, mtDNA per nuclear genome and per mitochondrial mass, evoked recruitment and respiratory recovery at successive time points after a measured S-vigabatrin pulse and washout. Two published WWOX cases had new symmetrical thalamic and pallidal MRI changes during treatment. Neither observation measures mitochondrial nucleotide pools. title: Zonisamide and astrocytic support in WWOX loss
opening_paragraph: **Candidate selection.** The existing WWOX dossier covers the antiseizure drug's multichannel activity and a co-treated WOREE case with persistent seizures. A separate question is whether zonisamide can increase astrocytic cystine exchange and provide a sustained increase in neuronal glutathione synthesis. In untreated WWOX tissue, the exchanger and glutamate-clearance transcripts fall together. Exchange releases glutamate, so both a benefit and a cost are plausible.
